claim: Epithelial tissues acquire their integrity and function through the apico-basal polarization of their constituent cells.
source: Epithelial tissues acquire their integrity and function through the apico-basal polarization of their constituent cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about epithelial tissue organization.

claim: Proteins of the PAR and Crumbs complexes are pivotal to epithelial polarization.
source: Proteins of the PAR and Crumbs complexes are pivotal to epithelial polarization
evidence: This is supported by established scientific consensus in the field.

claim: Polarity proteins organize in submicrometric clusters.
source: Proteins organize in submicrometric clusters
evidence: This is supported by STED microscopy imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: PAR3 overlaps with the tight junction (TJ).
source: PAR3 overlapping with the tight junction (TJ)
evidence: This is supported by STED imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β form segregated clusters that are apical of the TJ.
source: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β form segregated clusters that are apical of the TJ
evidence: This is supported by STED imaging and colocalization analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β are present in an alternated pattern related to actin organization.
source: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β form segregated clusters that are apical of the TJ and present in an alternated pattern related to actin organization
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data showing the relationship with actin structures.

claim: CRB3A is apical of the TJ and partially overlaps with other polarity proteins.
source: CRB3A is also apical of the TJ and partially overlaps with other polarity proteins.
evidence: This is supported by STED imaging and colocalization analysis.

claim: Of the numerous potential interactions identified between polarity proteins, only PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β are spatially relevant in the junctional area of mature epithelial cells.
source: Of the numerous potential interactions identified between polarity proteins, only PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β are spatially relevant in the junctional area of mature epithelial cells
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Epithelial cells coordinate their organization into a polarized sheet of cells.
source: In epithelial tissues, cells coordinate their organization into a polarized sheet of cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about epithelial tissue organization.

claim: Each epithelial cell acquires an apico-basal organization and specialized lateral junctions, namely, tight junctions (TJs, also known as zonula occludens), adherens junctions, and desmosomes.
source: Each cell acquires an apico-basal organization and specialized lateral junctions, namely, tight junctions (TJs, also known as zonula occludens), adherens junctions, and desmosomes (Farquhar and Palade, 1963).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Farquhar and Palade, 1963.

claim: The apico-basal organization and specialized lateral junctions are key to the development, maintenance, and function of epithelial tissues.
source: This organization is key to the development, maintenance, and function of epithelial tissues.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about epithelial tissue function.

claim: PAR3, PAR6, aPKC (PAR complex), Crumbs, PATJ, PALS1 (Crumbs complex), Scribble, LGL, and DLG (Scribble complex) are pivotal to epithelial polarization in mammals.
source: Over the past two decades, several proteins have been discovered to be pivotal to epithelial polarization, such as PAR3, PAR6, aPKC (PAR complex), Crumbs, PATJ, PALS1 (Crumbs complex), Scribble, LGL, and DLG (Scribble complex) in mammals (for review, see Assémat et al., 2008; Pickett et al., 2019; Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles (Assémat et al., 2008; Pickett et al., 2019; Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014).

claim: Polarity proteins are remarkably well conserved over the animal kingdom.
source: These proteins are remarkably well conserved over the animal kingdom (Belahbib et al., 2018; Le Bivic, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Belahbib et al., 2018 and Le Bivic, 2013.

claim: Deletion or depletion of polarity proteins usually results in dramatic developmental defects.
source: Deletion or depletion of one of these proteins usually results in dramatic developmental defects (Alarcon, 2010; Charrier et al., 2015; Hakanen et al., 2019; Lalli, 2012; Park et al., 2011; Sabherwal and Papalopulu, 2012; Tait et al., 2020; Whiteman et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies showing developmental defects.

claim: Polarity proteins interact to form multiprotein complexes.
source: We and others have found that these proteins interact to form multiprotein complexes.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge and previous research.

claim: The PAR complex consists of PAR3, PAR6, and aPKC proteins.
source: the PAR complex consisting of PAR3, PAR6, and aPKC proteins (Joberty et al., 2000; Lin et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Joberty et al., 2000 and Lin et al., 2000.

claim: The Crumbs complex consists of CRUMBS, PALS1, and PATJ.
source: the Crumbs complex consisting of CRUMBS, PALS1, and PATJ (Bhat et al., 1999; Makarova et al., 2003; Roh et al., 2002b)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bhat et al., 1999; Makarova et al., 2003; Roh et al., 2002b.

claim: The Scribble complex consists of Scribble, LGL, and DLG.
source: the Scribble complex consisting of Scribble, LGL, and DLG (Bilder et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bilder et al., 2000.

claim: Many interactions between proteins of different polarity complexes can occur.
source: However, this view became more complex over the years as many interactions between proteins of different complexes can occur (Assémat et al., 2008; Hurd et al., 2003; Lemmers et al., 2004)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Assémat et al., 2008; Hurd et al., 2003; Lemmers et al., 2004.

claim: Interactions of polarity proteins with cytoskeleton regulators and lateral junction proteins are common.
source: interactions of polarity proteins with cytoskeleton regulators and lateral junction proteins are common (Assémat et al., 2008; Chen and Macara, 2005; Itoh et al., 2001; Médina et al., 2002; Michel et al., 2005; Roh et al., 2002a; Takekuni et al., 2003; Tan et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to studies showing these interactions.

claim: There is no clear hierarchy of the importance of the numerous interactions between polarity proteins.
source: A current limitation in the understanding of polarization is that there is no clear hierarchy of the importance of these numerous interactions.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Potential interactions revealed through biochemical assays do not necessarily reflect relevant interactions in cells.
source: Potential interactions revealed through biochemical assays do not necessarily reflect relevant interactions in cells and do not specify when nor where in the cell these interactions could be relevant.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the limitations of biochemical assays.

claim: Polarity proteins are often found concentrated at the apical junction.
source: Polarity proteins have been localized with classical light microscopy, and remarkably, they are often found concentrated at the apical junction, a key organizational landmark of epithelial cells.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge from previous microscopy studies.

claim: The precise localization of polarity proteins at organizational landmarks is missing except for a few limited cases.
source: However, except for a few limited cases (Hirose et al., 2002; Izumi et al., 1998; Tan et al., 2020), the precise localization of polarity proteins at these organizational landmarks is missing.
evidence: This is an assessment of the current state of knowledge with citations to limited cases.

claim: The study used stimulated-emission-depletion (STED) microscopy to systematically localize polarity proteins.
source: To tackle these challenges, we decided to systematically localize with stimulated‐emission‐depletion (STED) microscopy the polarity proteins that are key to the establishment of the apical pole of epithelia: PAR3, aPKC, PAR6β, PATJ, PALS1, and CRB3A.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The study focused on mature epithelia because protein interactions and localization are likely stationary in this state.
source: Because how proteins interact and localize is likely to depend on cell differentiation, we decided to focus here on mature epithelia, a state where we hypothesize that protein interactions and localization are stationary.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about protein behavior in mature epithelia.

claim: The study used human and murine intestine and Caco-2 cells.
source: Using human and murine intestine and Caco-2 cells
evidence: This describes the biological samples used in the study.

claim: Polarity proteins localize in distinct subregions that do not reflect the canonical definition of polarity protein complexes.
source: We find that polarity proteins localize in distinct subregions that do not reflect the canonical definition of polarity protein complexes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the imaging and colocalization data.

claim: The localization of polarity proteins with respect to the cytoskeleton emphasizes emerging roles of polarity proteins as regulators of actin organization.
source: In addition, their localization with respect to the cytoskeleton emphasizes some emerging roles of polarity proteins as regulators of actin organization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed spatial relationships between polarity proteins and actin.

claim: STED images were acquired in the TJ region both in the apico-basal and the planar orientations of cells.
source: STED images were acquired in the TJ region both in the apico-basal and the planar orientations of cells in human and mouse intestinal biopsies (Figure 1) and Caco-2 cells (Figure 2).
evidence: This describes the imaging methodology used in the study.

claim: Samples were cryo-sectioned when needed to optimize sample orientation.
source: To optimize the sample orientation, samples were cryo-sectioned when needed, in particular to obtain apico-basal orientation.
evidence: This describes the sample preparation methodology.

claim: Intestinal cells were observed exclusively in villi.
source: Since we focused on mature epithelia, intestinal cells were observed exclusively in villi
evidence: This describes the specific tissue regions examined in the study.

claim: Caco-2 cells were seeded on filters and grown over 14 days to allow sufficient differentiation.
source: Caco-2 cells were seeded on filters and grown over 14 days to allow sufficient differentiation (Pinto et al., 1983).
evidence: This describes the cell culture methodology with citation to Pinto et al., 1983.

claim: The resolution of STED microscopy followed by deconvolution was about 80 nm in each color channel.
source: Because the resolution of STED microscopy followed by deconvolution was, in our hands, about 80 nm in each color channel
evidence: This describes the technical specifications of the imaging method.

claim: The gain of resolution compared to classical confocal microscopy approaches was threefold in the planar orientation and sevenfold along the apico-basal axis.
source: the gain of resolution compared to classical confocal microscopy approaches was threefold in the planar orientation and sevenfold along the apico‐basal axis.
evidence: This is a comparison of imaging resolution between STED and confocal microscopy.

claim: The localization of each polarity protein was conserved across all samples and species.
source: We found that the localization of each polarity protein was conserved across all samples and species (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: All polarity proteins were concentrated in the TJ region as clusters of typically 80–200 nm in size.
source: All proteins were concentrated in the TJ region as clusters of typically 80–200 nm in size (the smallest cluster size found is likely due to the imaging resolution limit)
evidence: This is supported by STED imaging data.

claim: PAR3 was mostly found at the TJs.
source: While we mostly found PAR3 at the TJs (Figures 1A, C, D, and F, 2A and C)
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: PAR6β and aPKC were at the TJ level and apical of the TJ.
source: PAR6β and aPKC were at the TJ level and apical of the TJ (Figures 1A and C and 2A and C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: CRB3A, PALS1, and PATJ were found almost exclusively apical of the TJ.
source: We found CRB3A, PALS1, and PATJ almost exclusively apical of the TJ (Figures 1A, C, D, and F, 2A and C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: PAR6β, aPKC, CRB3A, PALS1, and PATJ were often found separated laterally from the TJ, frequently detected as clusters 100–200 nm away from the TJ.
source: Interestingly, we often found PAR6β, aPKC, CRB3A, PALS1, and PATJ separated laterally from the TJ since we frequently detected clusters of these proteins 100–200 nm away from the TJ (Figures 1A, B, D, and E, 2A and E).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: CRB3A was more spread from the apical to the TJ domain in Caco-2 cells compared to intestinal samples.
source: There were some slight differences between intestinal samples and Caco-2 cells; in particular, CRB3A was more spread from the apical to the TJ domain in Caco-2 cells (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Differences in protein localization between intestinal samples and Caco-2 cells may originate from sample preparation or differences in cell organization due to tissue maturation.
source: These differences may originate from sample preparation or differences in cell organization due to tissue maturation.
evidence: This is speculation about the causes of observed differences.

claim: Polarity proteins organize in separate subdomains in the TJ region, namely, PAR3 at the TJ, and the other polarity proteins studied mostly apical of the TJ.
source: These first results show that polarity proteins organize in separate subdomains in the TJ region, namely, PAR3 at the TJ, and the other polarity proteins studied mostly apical of the TJ.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the imaging data.

claim: The observation that polarity proteins can organize as clusters has been reported in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: The observation that polarity proteins can organize as clusters has been reported in Caenorhabditis elegans (Dickinson et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dickinson et al., 2017 and Wang et al., 2017.

claim: A CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in Caco-2 cell line expressing PAR6β tagged with the fluorescent protein Citrine was prepared.
source: First, we prepared a CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in Caco-2 cell line expressing PAR6β tagged with the fluorescent protein Citrine (see 'Materials and methods' for preparation details).
evidence: This describes the methodology for creating a knock-in cell line.

claim: There is very good agreement between images of PAR6β observed live with Citrine or fixed with Alexa Fluor-568.
source: We find a very good agreement between images observed live with Citrine or fixed with Alexa Fluor-568 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: PAR6β organizes in clusters in live images.
source: In particular, we find that PAR6β organizes in clusters in live images
evidence: This is supported by live imaging data.

claim: Most clusters of PAR6β found with live imaging can be found again with immunolabeling.
source: most clusters found with live imaging can be found again with immunolabeling.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of live and fixed imaging data.

claim: Permeabilization using freeze-and-thaw or detergent leads to very similar results for PATJ localization.
source: Images obtained with this protocol or the one using detergent gave comparable results.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Clusters of PATJ can be observed without the use of detergent.
source: Clusters of proteins can also be observed without the use of detergent.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data using freeze-thaw permeabilization.

claim: The clustered organization of proteins observed is not due to methodological artifacts.
source: We conclude that the clustered organization of proteins we observe is not due to methodological artifacts as we can find the same clusters of PAR6β proteins in live and fixed CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in Caco-2 cells, and the absence of detergent when staining cells with antibodies against PATJ does lead to the same organization as the one observed with detergent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the validation experiments.

claim: PALS1 colocalizes strongly with PATJ.
source: First, we found that some of the proteins colocalize strongly: PALS1 with PATJ
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: aPKC colocalizes strongly with PAR6β.
source: First, we found that some of the proteins colocalize strongly: PALS1 with PATJ and aPKC with PAR6β
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β are well segregated from each other when observed in the planar orientation.
source: Surprisingly, we found PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β well segregated from each other when we observed them in the planar orientation.
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β sometimes appear as alternating bands along the junction with a spatial repeat in the range of 200–300 nm.
source: They sometimes appeared as alternating bands along the junction with a spatial repeat in the range of 200–300 nm (zooms in Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Alternating bands of PALS1-PATJ and aPKC-PAR6β sometimes seem formed by clusters facing each other in neighboring cells, indicating potential coordination of polarity protein organization between adjacent cells.
source: In some cases, these bands seemed formed by clusters facing each other in neighboring cells, indicating potential coordination of polarity protein organization between adjacent cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed spatial patterns.

claim: Only a minority of CRB3A colocalized with any of the other polarity proteins.
source: Second, we found that only a minority of CRB3A colocalized with any of the other polarity proteins (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: CRB3A has been reported to strongly interact both with PALS1 and PAR6.
source: These observations are also surprising because CRB3A has been reported to strongly interact both with PALS1 and PAR6 (Hayase et al., 2013; Lemmers et al., 2004; Li et al., 2014; Makarova et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The interactions between CRB3A and PALS1/PAR6 may be mostly transient or not prominent in the TJ area.
source: This could mean that these interactions are mostly transient or that they are not prominent in the TJ area.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of CRB3A interactions based on the colocalization data.

claim: The result questions the stability and functional cellular meaning of the canonical CRB3-PALS1-PATJ complex and the CRB3-PAR6 interaction.
source: This result questions the stability and functional cellular meaning of the canonical CRB3-PALS1-PATJ complex and the CRB3-PAR6 interaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: PAR3 is hardly found with PALS1 or aPKC.
source: Finally, when localizing PAR3 along with PALS1 or aPKC, we found that PAR3 is hardly found with either of these proteins (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: PAR3, aPKC, and PAR6β do not associate in a static complex.
source: These data show that PAR3, aPKC, and PAR6β do not associate in a static complex as has been suggested in several non-mammalian models (Afonso and Henrique, 2006; Harris and Peifer, 2005; Morais-de-Sá et al., 2010; Rodriguez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data, contrasting with previous models.

claim: aPKC and PAR6β are likely linked in the apical TJ region, whereas PAR3 is poorly associated with them.
source: It appears, in our conditions, that aPKC and PAR6β are likely linked in the apical TJ region, whereas PAR3 is poorly associated with them.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: The interaction between PAR3 and PAR6β-aPKC may be mostly transient or not relevant in the TJ area.
source: Again, it is possible that the interaction between PAR3 and PAR6β-aPKC is mostly transient or that it is not relevant in the TJ area.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of PAR3 interactions based on the colocalization data.

claim: PAR3 is largely excluded from other polarity proteins at the TJ.
source: We conclude that PAR3 is largely excluded from other polarity proteins at the TJ
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: PALS1-PATJ, PAR6β-aPKC, and CRB3 form three spatially separated entities in the apical region of the TJ.
source: We conclude that PAR3 is largely excluded from other polarity proteins at the TJ and that PALS1-PATJ, PAR6β-aPKC, and CRB3 form three spatially separated entities in the apical region of the TJ.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: In the canonical Crumbs complex, PALS1 binds to the transmembrane protein CRB3A and PATJ binds to PALS1.
source: In the generally accepted description of the canonical Crumbs complex, PALS1 binds to the transmembrane protein CRB3A and PATJ binds to PALS1 (Roh et al., 2002b).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature, supported by citation to Roh et al., 2002b.

claim: PALS1 and PATJ are thought to be in close vicinity of the membrane since CRB3A is a short transmembrane protein.
source: Therefore, PALS1 and PATJ are thought to be in close vicinity of the membrane since CRB3A is a short transmembrane protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the canonical model of the Crumbs complex.

claim: It was proposed that PATJ links CRB3A-PALS1 to the TJ area because of the direct interaction of PATJ with the TJ protein ZO-3 and Claudin1.
source: Moreover, it was proposed that PATJ links CRB3A-PALS1 to the TJ area (Michel et al., 2005) because of the direct interaction of PATJ with the TJ protein ZO-3 and Claudin1 (Roh et al., 2002a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Michel et al., 2005 and Roh et al., 2002a.

claim: Most PATJ proteins are often too far from the TJ to interact with this structure.
source: our localization of PATJ with STED suggests that most PATJ proteins are often too far from the TJ to interact with this structure (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by STED imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: PATJ was observed with electron tomography using immunogold labeling in Caco-2 cells.
source: Therefore, to obtain a more complete understanding of PATJ localization in the TJ region, we observed PATJ with electron tomography using immunogold labeling in Caco-2 cells (Figure 5).
evidence: This describes the methodology used for electron microscopy.

claim: PATJ was often found organized in clusters apical of the TJ.
source: Consistent with what we observed with STED, we often found PATJ organized in clusters apical of the TJ (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by electron tomography data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Most PATJ proteins were about 80 nm away from the TJ.
source: We found that most PATJ proteins were about 80 nm away from the TJ (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of electron tomography data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Most PATJ molecules do not interact directly with TJ proteins.
source: Therefore, our data suggest that most PATJ molecules do not interact directly with TJ proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the distance measurements.

claim: Most PATJ proteins were close to the apical membrane.
source: We found instead most PATJ proteins were close to the apical membrane and that only a small fraction was present in microvilli or the cytoplasm (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by electron tomography data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Only a small fraction of PATJ was present in microvilli or the cytoplasm.
source: We found instead most PATJ proteins were close to the apical membrane and that only a small fraction was present in microvilli or the cytoplasm (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by electron tomography data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Previous observations that PATJ associates with ZO-3 or Claudin1 might depend on the cellular state, or these interactions could be transient.
source: Previous observations that PATJ associates with ZO-3 or Claudin1 might depend on the cellular state, or these interactions could be transient.
evidence: This is speculation about the nature of PATJ interactions based on the distance measurements.

claim: It is unlikely that CRB3A anchors most PALS1 and PATJ molecules to the plasma membrane.
source: CRB3A is thought to anchor PALS1 and PATJ to the plasma membrane. However, given our results showing a minor colocalization of PATJ and PALS1 with CRB3A, it is unlikely to be the case for most PALS1 and PATJ molecules.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: 73% of gold particles labeling PATJ were less than 38 nm away from the plasma membrane, compatible with the association of PATJ and PALS1 with the apical plasma membrane.
source: we measured the distance of the immunogold label of PATJ to the plasma membrane (Figure 5E) and found that the distance of the gold label is in most cases compatible with the association of PATJ and PALS1 with the apical plasma membrane (123/169 ≈ 73% of gold particles were less than 38 nm away from the plasma membrane, corresponding to the size of the primary and gold-labeled secondary antibody combination added with the size of PALS1).
evidence: This is supported by quantification of electron tomography data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: PATJ and PALS1 are likely to be anchored to the apical membrane not by CRB3A but by yet unknown apical membrane proteins.
source: We conclude that PATJ and PALS1 are likely to be anchored to the apical membrane not by CRB3A but by yet unknown apical membrane proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the electron tomography data and colocalization analysis.

claim: In the region where PATJ, PALS1, PAR6β, and aPKC are located, the actin cytoskeleton consists mostly of microvilli structures.
source: We find that in the region where PATJ, PALS1, PAR6β, and aPKC are located, the actin cytoskeleton identified with 3D STED consists mostly of microvilli structures (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: PATJ and PALS1 are found mostly at the base of microvilli or in between microvilli.
source: PATJ and PALS1 are found mostly at the base of microvilli or in between microvilli (Figure 6)
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data shown in Figure 6.

claim: PAR6β and aPKC are mostly found within microvilli or close to the base of microvilli, but hardly between microvilli.
source: PAR6β and aPKC are mostly found within microvilli or close to the base of microvilli, but hardly between microvilli (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The different locations of PATJ-PALS1 and PAR6β-aPKC within the apical region reinforces the observation that they form separate clusters.
source: This result reinforces our previous observations that PATJ-PALS1 and PAR6β-aPKC form separate clusters as we find them at different locations within the apical region of the junction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the 3D STED imaging data.

claim: All polarity proteins studied organize as submicrometric clusters concentrated in the TJ region.
source: We found the following (Figure 7): (1) all these polarity proteins organize as submicrometric clusters concentrated in the TJ region.
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging data.

claim: PAR3 localizes at the TJ.
source: PAR3 localizes at the TJ
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging data.

claim: aPKC and PAR6β localize at the TJ level, but mostly apically of the TJ.
source: aPKC, and PAR6β localize at the TJ level, but mostly apically of the TJ
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging data.

claim: PATJ, PALS1, and CRB3A are apical of the TJ.
source: while PATJ, PALS1, and CRB3A are apical of the TJ (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a summary of the imaging data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: PAR6β-aPKC and PATJ-PALS1 form two pairs that are often respectively found in the same clusters.
source: (2) PAR6β-aPKC and PATJ-PALS1 form two pairs that are often respectively found in the same clusters (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PAR6β-aPKC and PATJ-PALS1 form a stable and major complex in the TJ region.
source: strongly indicating that these respective proteins form a stable and major complex in this region of the cells (i.e., the PAR6-aPKC complex and the PALS1-PATJ complex).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and PAR6β-aPKC clusters are segregated from each other.
source: (3) Unexpectedly, PALS1-PATJ and PAR6β-aPKC clusters are segregated from each other (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: PALS1-PATJ and PAR6β-aPKC clusters are concentrated in the first one or two rows of microvilli.
source: Our data show that these clusters are concentrated in the first one or two rows of microvilli
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data.

claim: The PAR6β-aPKC complex is localized at the base and within microvilli.
source: with the PAR6β-aPKC complex localized at the base and within microvilli
evidence: This is supported by 3D STED imaging data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The PALS1-PATJ complex is localized at the base and in between microvilli.
source: whereas the PALS1-PATJ complex is localized at the base and in between these microvilli (Figures 5 and 6)
evidence: This is supported by electron tomography and 3D STED imaging data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The PAR6β-aPKC complex and the PALS1-PATJ complex are spatially separated in the cell.
source: further showing that the PAR6β-aPKC complex and the PALS1-PATJ complex are spatially separated in the cell.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 3D STED imaging data.

claim: CRB3 shows little association with any of the other polarity proteins.
source: (4) CRB3 shows little association with any of the other polarity proteins (Figure 4B)
evidence: This is supported by colocalization analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The little association of CRB3 with other polarity proteins questions how PALS1-PATJ and PAR6β-aPKC are mechanistically recruited to the plasma membrane and localized to the apical surface.
source: questioning how PALS1-PATJ and PAR6β-aPKC are mechanistically recruited to the plasma membrane and localized to the apical surface.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization data.

claim: Most previous studies on polarity protein interactions used overexpression to identify interactors.
source: Notably, most of these previous studies used overexpression to identify the interactors of a given protein
evidence: This is an assessment of previous methodologies in the field.

claim: Overexpression might have introduced biases in some cases in previous studies.
source: this methodological limitation might have introduced biases in some cases.
evidence: This is speculation about potential limitations of previous studies.

claim: Previous studies concluded that PAR6β can interact with PAR3, aPKC, PALS1, PATJ, and CRB3A.
source: If we focus only on proteins observed in this article, these studies concluded that PAR6β can interact with PAR3, aPKC, PALS1, PATJ, and CRB3A
evidence: This is a summary of previous findings from the literature.

claim: Previous studies concluded that aPKC can additionally interact with PAR3.
source: aPKC can additionally interact with PAR3
